## Episode Thesis

Pengepodden episode with DNB Carnegie oil and energy analyst Helge André Martinsen on the energy market as the Strait of Hormuz stays partly closed. Oil has balanced better than feared: China cut imports, the US released stock, and Brent sits around $90. The squeeze has hit refined products instead, with record diesel and jet fuel cracks and record refining margins. European gas storage is at record lows going into winter. Short term, prices face upward pressure while stocks keep drawing. Over 12-18 months the guest sees heavy downside risk for oil (a fraying OPEC and possible oversupply in 2027) and for gas (a wave of new LNG capacity), so he finds the risk/reward unattractive and tells investors to stay nimble.
